newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt and crown firms, awaiting U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt and crown firms, awaiting U.S. data.

text.p: Swedish debt yields inched down a touch in the early session Thursday and the crown continued to firm, led by foreign markets, dealers said.
The market was waiting for U.S. second quarter GDP data due at 1230 GMT.

"There is a strong momentum on the downside. We're not at Wednesday's lowest levels yet, but we're not far from it. It's totally foreign driven and we are now sidelined ahead of the U.S. GDP," one dealer said.
Six-month T-bill rates were down one basis point to 4.28 percent and the ten-year bond yields shed one to 6.38 percent.
The crown firmed against the dollar and the mark.
At 1045 it stood at 7.9355 to the dollar compared to 7.9971 late on Wednesday while the crown was trading at 4.3280 to the mark from 4.3385.
Sweden's central bank, Riksbank, held a board meeting but no changes were announced to interest rates. The market had not expected any moves.
